source.title: Binarized Neural Machine Translation
source.authors: Yi-Chi Zhang; Ankush Garg; Yuan Cao; Lukasz Lew; B. Ghorbani; Zhi-Ru Zhang; O. Firat

record.tranche_reason: Extends scaling-law measurements to machine-translation models, including weight-binarized Transformers, and evaluates in-domain and out-of-domain translation data.
record.gate_note: The paper fits loss-scaling curves and reports encoder and decoder exponents across evaluation datasets. It also reports downstream BLEU and BLEURT trends. WMT binarization ablations and cited results are not scaling-law results and are not included.
record.test_reason: The study fits a power law of per-token translation loss against encoder and decoder parameter counts. It covers float and weight-binarized encoder-decoder machine-translation Transformers (12 depths each) on a 3B-pair corpus, with 11 evaluation sets. This is a new setting for the scaling-law form (V5) and for exponent variation (V7). It also reports BLEU and BLEURT improving with size (V6).
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that weight-binarized Transformers scale like float ones, with exponents only slightly lower (e.g. p_e 0.16 vs 0.18, p_d 0.28 vs 0.31 in-domain), and generalize as well out of domain. They note a constant loss gap on production data. Larger binary models improve BLEU and BLEURT and can match smaller float models with fewer bits.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a machine-translation scaling setup with encoder- and decoder-depth sweeps and a fitted encoder/decoder parameter-count loss equation, comparing float and weight-binarized models; it does not reproduce the original language-model parameter/token/compute setup.
record.method_sensitivity: Fitted exponents differ across evaluation datasets and between float and weight-binarized models.

fits_no_version.finding: Training loss and in-domain test loss lie on one straight line for binary and float models, overlapping near 0.95–1.0. A 6L42L binary model (195M bits) matches the loss of a 6L8L float model (832M bits).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: At equal training loss, weight-binarized and float MT models generalize equally, so binarization shifts loss per parameter but not generalization.

record.code_released: Implementation in JAX/Flax will be open sourced; no URL stated
record.problems: The scaling-law study is limited to weight-binarized models and machine translation. It does not test token or compute scaling, compute-optimal allocation, or extrapolation from small runs to much larger runs. Uncertainty estimates are not reported.
record.rows_left_out: No results bearing on the tested versions were left out.

untested.parts: Not language-model pretraining loss. Data and compute scaling are not varied, and the parameter range is roughly 50M–200M, about one order of magnitude.
No extrapolation from small runs checked against larger runs.
Only depth is scaled; no comparison of shapes at fixed parameter count.
Other modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning and transfer; data and compute scaling in MT.
Downstream predicted from loss; tasks other than translation; any fitted downstream scaling curve.
Parameter-counting conventions, fitting method, training schedule as deliberate variables; curvature away from a power law.

missing.what: Decoder-scaling generation quality: binary BLEU is 2–3 points below float at the same depth, and MBR-BLEURT improves with sample size.
A loss gap between binary and float models at the same parameter count on in-house data, which the WMT experiments did not show.

record.verdict_notes: Machine translation is a supervised seq2seq setting, not LM pretraining, so it is linked to V5, not V1. The scaling range is narrow: depth 6–48 at width 512, about 50M–200M parameters. The record's exponents for the five WMT datasets (S25–S44) are shifted or scrambled relative to Table 3 and have been corrected. The Wikipedia binary p_e differs between Figure 2b (0.13) and Table 3 (0.12). The record's V6 limits_scope label (binary 2–3 BLEU worse) was dropped: an offset between model classes does not qualify downstream predictability. Binary and float models were trained for different numbers of epochs (9 vs 5).

versions.untested_parts: The study measures machine-translation loss, not held-out language-model pretraining loss; it does not separately test token- or compute-scaling.
It fits curves to size sweeps but does not report predictions made from smaller runs and checked against much larger runs.
No fixed-compute-budget allocation between parameters and tokens is tested.
The study scales depth but does not compare architectures at fixed parameter count.
Tests machine translation and weight binarization, not other modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer.
Reports translation BLEU and BLEURT trends with model size, but does not test a general downstream-task relationship or predict downstream results from pretraining loss.

Reports exponent variation across evaluation datasets and float versus binary models; does not vary parameter-count conventions, fitting methods, or schedules to test their effects, nor report curves bending away from a power law.

rows.operation_detail: Evaluates beam-search BLEU across model sizes
rows.baseline: Float models at the same depth are 2–3 BLEU points higher; 10L6L float comparison

rows.note: Trend and comparison are described in text; exact plotted scores are not stated.
rows.check: Only a monotonic improvement of BLEU with size is described. No fitted or predicted downstream trend is given, so 'predictable' rests on the qualitative trend only.

rows.value: BLEURT improves as model size increases; larger sample size also improves quality
rows.note: Text says 64 samples approximately match float-model quality; exact plotted scores are not stated.
rows.check: Only a qualitative statement that BLEURT improves with size; values are figure-only.

relationships.condition: Float and weight-binarized encoder-decoder MT Transformers, encoder and decoder depth scaling, in-domain and 10 OOD evaluation sets
relationships.reason: The power law in encoder and decoder parameters fits with R2 of 99.5–99.8 on ID and Wikipedia (S01–S04, S21–S24). Fitted exponents are reported for all sets (S05–S20, S25–S44).
relationships.display_finding: Parameter-based power laws achieved reported R² values of 99.5–99.8 on in-domain and Wikipedia evaluations, with fitted exponents across all evaluated distributions.

relationships.condition: Encoder-scaling binary and float MT models on the in-domain test set (beam-search BLEU and MBR-BLEURT)
relationships.reason: BLEU consistently improves with binary model size (D01), and BLEURT improves with model size (D02). The evidence is qualitative and from figures only.
relationships.display_finding: BLEU consistently improved with binary model size, and BLEURT also improved as model size increased.

relationships.condition: Exponents compared across evaluation datasets and between float and weight-binarized models
relationships.reason: Table 3 exponents vary by evaluation set: float p_e 0.12–0.24 and p_d 0.18–0.37. Binary exponents are mostly slightly lower (S01–S44, values corrected per Table 3).
relationships.display_finding: Floating-point encoder exponents range from 0.12 to 0.24 and decoder exponents from 0.18 to 0.37 across evaluation sets, while binary-model exponents are mostly slightly lower.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Float and weight-binarized machine-translation models across the reported in-domain and OOD datasets
reader_labels.reason: The study reports fitted loss-scaling exponents for both model classes across datasets, with high fit R2 values stated for the in-domain and Wikipedia examples; see S01–S44.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Binary encoder-scaling models on the in-domain test set
reader_labels.reason: The text reports that BLEU and BLEURT improve as model size increases; see D01–D02.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Binary and float models compared at the same depth
reader_labels.reason: Binary models are reported to be 2–3 BLEU points worse at the same depth, despite larger binary models reaching a comparable score; see D01.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Exponent comparisons across float and binary models and evaluation datasets
reader_labels.reason: Reported fitted exponents vary across dataset and model type, while the study describes the binary exponents as only slightly below the float exponents for the main comparison; see S01–S44.
